differences.what: Rectangle extension uses the kernel's proportion mode instead of an absolute distance. Old: extend_equally(pline, seg, 0.15) = dist 0.15, proportion 0 -> unitized direction * 0.15 on both ends (351933c:cgal_polyline_util.cpp:464-486, 'proportion != 0 ? scale by vector : unitize*dist'). Current: base[3].extend_segment_equally(0, 0.15*1.0, 0.15*1.0) where the kernel signature is (segment_id, dist, proportion) (polyline.h:197) and proportion=0.15 != 0 selects the proportional branch p0 -= v*0.15, p1 += v*0.15 with v the un-normalized segment vector (polyline.cpp:1286-1301). Side segments 0 and 2 of rings 3/4 (p2->p1, p13->p14) have length 2a = 0.55 at shift 0.5, so each end moves 0.0825 instead of 0.15. Vertical segments 1 and 3 (p1->p13, p14->p2) have length z = 0.5, and extend_segment_equally(1, 0.6, 0.6) moves each end 0.3 instead of 0.6. The side-face rebuild at cr_c_ip_core.h:94-115 inherits these points, so all four slice_projectsheer side faces and the four mill_project faces differ from 2024. Fix: call extend_segment_equally(seg, dist) with proportion left 0.

shift parameter dropped from the public factory: old geometry depends on joint.shift (user-set per family row); current cr_c_ip_2() takes none and reads the JointPlate::shift member default 0.5. Same geometry at the default only.

family.insertion_direction: OLD: cross joints are detected by plane_to_face (351933c:cmake/src/wood/include/wood_main.cpp:280-458, type=30 at :293). The outline of each plate is intersected with the two face planes of the other plate giving four segments cx0_py0, cx0_py1, cx1_py0, cx1_py1 (:329-348), all oriented like the first (:358-363). The middle line c of cx0_py1 and cx1_py0 is scaled x10 (:376-378); every segment start/end is projected onto c, lMin is the shortest overlap (from the last start to the first end) and lMax the full span (:381-399). midPlane passes through lMin's midpoint with lMin's direction as normal (:405-407); joint_area is midPlane cut with the four segments (:430). v = vector from midPlane∩lMax to the farther end of lMax (:416-417), lengthened by JOINT_VOLUME_EXTENSION[2] when positive (:421-426). joint_volumes[0] = joint_area + v, joint_volumes[1] = joint_area − v (:436-437); volumes [2],[3] are never set for type 30, so orient_to_connection_area builds xform0 from volumes [0],[1] and xform1 again from [0],[1] (351933c:cmake/src/wood/include/wood_joint.cpp:342-346), applying xform0 to m[0],m[1] and xform1 to f[0],f[1] (:248-267). The unit joint's z axis therefore maps onto ±v, i.e. along the intersection line of the two plates (the direction of c / lMax), pointing from the mid plane toward the far end: cr_c_ip_0's female slot occupies z∈[0,1] and the male slot z∈[-1,0] (351933c:...wood_joint_lib.cpp:4588-4598), so each plate is slotted from an opposite end of the crossing line. An exploded picture moves plate a along +v and plate b along −v (v = volumes[0].centroid − polygon.centroid). CURRENT: WoodSession::compute_cross_contact -> plane_to_face (src/joinery_solver/wood_session.cpp:522-543; src/joinery_solver/wood_algorithms/wood_contact_detection.cpp:622-...): same four segments oriented by dot with the first (:697-703), middle line c scaled 10 (:705-710), parameters cpt0/cpt1/cpt, lMin, lMax (:715-735), midPlane through lMin.center() with normal lMin direction (:737-749), v from midPlane∩lMax to the farther lMax end with optional extension[2] (:751-771), polygon = plane_4lines (:773-780), result.volumes[0] = polygon + v, [1] = polygon − v (:786-787), lines[0..1] from the polygon mid-points (:783-784). JointPlate::orient(InteractionContactCross) copies lines[0..1] and volumes[0..1] into joint_volumes[0],[1] with joint_type 30 (src/joinery_solver/wood_elements/wood_element_joint_plate.cpp:719-742); joint_orient_to_connection_area maps male outlines by Xform::from_change_of_basis(vols[0], vols[1]) and female by the same xform when vols[2],[3] are absent (src/joinery_solver/wood_algorithms/wood_feature_construction.cpp:102-120). Same definition as 2024: insertion along ±v, the plates' intersection line. Derivable in a picture from InteractionContactCross::volumes[0]/[1] and ::polygon, or from InteractionFeaturePlate::joint_volumes[0]/[1]. Only orientation-stage divergence: 2024 applied joint.scale (settings scale, default {1,1,1}) to all outlines before the change of basis (351933c:wood_joint.cpp:326-333); the port stores joint.scale (wood_element_joint_plate.cpp:562, :878) but never applies it (grep over src/joinery_solver finds only assignments) — no effect at the default.
family.notes: Verification scope: every claim read from the cited files; nothing was built or run (READ-ONLY). Family-wide facts: (1) The dominant defect is in cr_c_ip_core.h:40-47 and affects cr_c_ip_2, _3, _4, _5 identically: Polyline::extend_segment_equally(segment_id, dist, proportion) (session_cpp/src/polyline.h:197) receives ext*factor_a as dist and ext*factor_b as proportion; a non-zero proportion makes the kernel scale by the raw segment vector and ignore dist (polyline.cpp:1286-1301), while 2024 extend_equally(pline, seg, dist) had proportion 0 and moved both ends by |dist| along the unit direction (351933c:cgal_polyline_util.cpp:464-486). At the default shift (s=0.225, a=0.275) the side segments of rings 3/4 are 0.55 long and the vertical ones 0.5, so the port extends 0.0825/0.3 where 2024 extended 0.15/0.6; cr_c_ip_5 additionally loses its +0.27 / -0.075 asymmetry. Correct form: base[k].extend_segment_equally(0, 0.15*fa); (2, 0.15*fb); (1, 0.6); (3, 0.6) with proportion left at 0, where fa/fb are 1/1 for 2..4 and 1.8/-0.5 for 5. (2) Everything else in cr_c_ip_core matches 2024 line by line: the 16-point layout (core:22-27 vs lib:4733-4739), v0 (core:29-31 vs lib:4741), the five rings (core:34-38 vs lib:4749-4755), offsets {0.5,0.4,0.4,0.4,0.4} by the ring normal (core:54,62-74 vs lib:4793-4805), rotation by axes (0,1,0),(1,0,0),(0,0,-1) (core:55 vs lib:4791), duplication of every polyline (core:83-92 vs lib:4829-4842), the side-face rebuild for ids 2 and 4 (core:94-115 vs lib:4848-4864), and identical male/female type lists (core:117-120). (3) Default parameters: 2024 shift default 0.5 (wood_joint.h:94), overridable per family via JOINTS_PARAMETERS_AND_TYPES[row*3+1]; current family path reads the same slot (wood_element_joint_plate.cpp:467, :571) and the factory path uses JointPlate::shift default 0.5 (h:40, cpp:879), but only cr_c_ip_1 exposes shift in its factory although 2..5 depend on it. divisions and unit_scale are unused by this family in both versions (unit_scale only for types 12/13: cpp:564-568, :886-887). (4) Plate application: 2024 merge_joints dispatches on the point count of outline index [1] of the face (351933c:wood_element.cpp:774): 5 points -> case (5) rectangle insertion using outline .front() (:1049-1073); drill lines are later in the list and never reach the merge; hole/drill type checks at :1374 and :42. Current MergeModifier::insert_side_joints does the same: marker = outlines[0][1].point_count(); 5 -> insert_rectangle_cut with outlines[0][0]/[1][0] (src/joinery_solver/wood_algorithms/wood_merge_modifier.cpp:394-397, 160-180). Because the library duplicates every polyline, [1] is the centre rectangle in both, so every cr_c_ip design is merged as the centre slot; the remaining rings/drills are exported as fabrication geometry only. (5) Current example examples/elements/element_joint_plate_cr_c_ip.cpp:11-18 builds cr_c_ip_0..5 on two 400x200x40 plates (:25-42) via compute_cross_contact + orient(contact, {first, second}) (:47-48); cr_c_ip_custom is not exercised by any example. 2024 cross tests (351933c:wood_test.cpp:2951-3522, e.g. type_plates_name_cross_corners :3016-3077) only set JOINT_VOLUME_EXTENSION[1]=2 and leave the joint types to the default (cr_c_ip_0 via the family default). (6) Unverified: whether the viewer-side consumers (drill_axes at wood_element_joint_plate.cpp:779-797, BRep cutting) treat slice_projectsheer / mill_project rings of cross joints the way the 2024 beam exporter did; not in scope of the geometry audit.
